risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- The imposition of reciprocal tariffs by the United States - one of the largest markets for textile exports - in April, followed by a further increase in August, led to substantial disruptions in textile exports and adversely impacted the industry.
- The West Asia Crisis lifted global crude oil prices, sharply raising synthetic fibre prices and the prices of dyes, chemicals, packing materials and fuel; yarn manufacturers were able to pass on only a part of this abnormal increase to consumers, compressing margins.
- Demand for synthetic yarn remained subdued through the year, cutting Textile Division production to 3,790 MT from 4,065 MT; management states the outlook for the synthetic value chain in the current year remains challenging owing to persistent subdued demand.
- Management explicitly flags that ongoing geopolitical situations - the West Asia Crisis and the outbreak of the war in Iran - create volatility and uncertainty in global trade that may adversely impact the Divisions' performance.
- Indian tea production rose about 5% to 1,370 million kgs, improving supply and pulling average auction prices in North India down by around Rs. 22 per kg; the Division's realisation fell by Rs. 13 per kg despite its quality focus, showing the segment's exposure to an industry-wide price cycle it does not control.
- The Division's order flow rests on ongoing expansion and upgradation initiatives of a concentrated set of large steel, infrastructure and industrial groups (Reliance Industries, JSW, Tata Steel, ArcelorMittal Nippon Steel, Vedanta, Adani Group, SAIL, RINL, Jindal Stainless, Jindal Ferrous), so a pause in that investment cycle would directly hit the Division.
- The Property Division operates against what management describes as challenging market conditions in the commercial real estate sector; its revenue depends on sustaining occupancy and renewing tenancies at enhanced rental rates.
- Tea and macadamia output at the Malawi step-down subsidiary NTEL both declined year on year (tea 1.71 million kgs from 1.75 million kgs; macadamia 2.15 million kgs from 2.23 million kgs), and the direct Mauritius subsidiary remained loss-making at the pre-tax level with no significant operational activity.
